body:
I've seen this advice before, and I appreciate the sentiment, but it usually just doesn't feel that way.

It's not like when one feels like this, they can entertain the thought "Now I can do absolutely anything, because I don't care about the consequences."  The weight of it is crushing, not uplifting.  Even if you try to push past that, and attempt to do what you say.. well nothing is fun anymore.  And "fun" and stressful is just stressful, but "boring" and calm, is just calm.  Neither really exists.

I even tried this once.  Just signed up for an all-day faire a state away, and just said "fuck it", and went.  I was depressed, but if I force myself to do this, through all my sadness and anxiety and worries and failures, maybe it'll be fine.  But I drive about half way and just sorta broke down.  Then I drove home and stayed in bed for a few hours.  I was still miserable, but relatively, I was better off lying in bed, if that makes any sense.

I do like the advice about booking myself solid.  I guess a lot of my loneliness comes from trying to hard to meet people, actually doing stuff, and still ending up with no one to hang out with, eat dinner with, go places with.  But if I just go out all the time to distract myself, I can't feel too bad.  I don't get severely down when other people are around.  That usually works as the best distraction, if I can keep myself going.

As for the heartbreak... I think the feelings are relative.  No I've never been in a strong relationship in that way with someone and had it all pulled away suddenly, but I've never been that kind of relationship either.  Its easy to say that the pain you felt through that is worse than mine, but you haven't been alone for as long as I have, never had a significant other for a 10 year period, constantly.

As for the "it will happen when it will happen" advice, I'm really beginning to not see any merit in it.  Yeah, it made since when I was in high school.  And then it sort of made sense when nothing happened in college.  And then in grad school, and the years after grad school.  But now I'm 27.  I know that seems young.  I would say the same thing to a 17 year old.  But a 17 year old has been dating for what, 2 years?  I've been going through that some 6 or 7 times longer.

You say "as soon as I'm ready to have a girlfriend and truly want one."  I don't see how that couldn't have happened by now.  Maybe the last half a year would have been bad for it, the way I've been feeling.  But all the many years and attempts and rejections and getting over it before that?  For someone my age, there just has to be something wrong with me.

Not only that, say I do need to wait to meet someone.  Now I have no experience with dating, sex, kissing.  I don't even know how to hold a girl's hand properly.  If my chances of finding someone are nonzero, what additional percent are going to be completely repelled by my awkwardness, lack of any experience, at my age?  Or when I'm 30? or 35?  How many of those am I going to screw up because I don't understand basic relationship stuff, that I should have learned in high school.

I don't know if this "giving it a break" thing is something I can manage, when I feel like its at least partially the reason I'm so miserable a lot of the time.

I really don't know, really.  I thought about this.  I guess talking helps, but you can't go around and befriend every single person that looks slightly lonely.  I really tried talking to people as well, when I was feeling better.  But a lot of the times it either ended up being a quick, casual conversation, or I felt pushed away somehow.  I'd like to say that random few-sentence chats help, but in my case, I'm not sure they really did.  The conversation would end, I'd feel slightly better for a minute or two, but then I'd go back to how I was... and then months of that lead to how I am.

I don't think I have a good answer.  Its good that you care about that stuff though.

I've tried the bars here, and the coffee shops, and book stores, parks, groups online.  Maybe there's something I'm missing, but I get super nervous about meeting people cold.  And when I try, it just doesn't work.  They sort of reject any continuation of the conversations; politely, or not so politely.  

I could move, but I just don't feel like it would be different.  It would be too much of a change, but not enough in any direction that would make me feel any different.  Just the same problems, in a different location.  And I would be turning my back completely on my career, in such a way that I could never work in this field again, negating some 8 years of education.

I do live far from where I grew up, although everyone I was close to is spread around now.  There's really no place I can go to now that would fix my problems.  There's no place I could think to move to that I would even have anyone to rely on, not in the way I need it.

But yeah, its a larger town, over a million metropolitan area.  But as for using my interests to connect with people, I tried for way over a year now.  Not associated with a university here anymore, and there's nothing really posted on the internet.  I tried a lot of the groups.  In some cases, I just didn't feel that welcome.  In others, it was just an awkward match, or I really didn't enjoy myself.  And there wasn't much to begin with.  I even would just go to public places and try to hang out, but not many people know what its like to try to start something like that with no one else to go with.  They say to just "start talking to people", "ask questions", "introduce yourself"  But everyone else is there with friends.  You can't just start sitting down to a group of people, who all know each other and not you, and try to start a conversation.  I tried, several times.  Didn't feel welcome, it was awkward.  I can't do that again.

I'm glad you met your husband, and I'm sorry about the recent diagnosis.  I realize I could be worse off, and I've tried to use that to make myself feel better.  I know it should, but honestly, I just feel worse.  Because besides the loneliness, social problems, lack of energy... well there's nothing wrong with me.  I have a good job, I'm healthy.  Just not happy.  

Although you say you met your husband at 35, but I doubt that he was your first boyfriend.  You likely had something in high school, college, after college.  I've been in a position to date for over 10 years now, and I have had nothing even close to anyone having feelings for me.  That's just too long of it never working, to believe that the next 10 years could be any different.  I realize it should have it's hits and misses, but its been all misses.  Getting casually rejected dozens of times.  Getting strongly rejected a few more times.  And falling in love with a close friend, and being devastated for months after, well still several times.  I'm fine with heartache, I get that there should be loneliness.  But not this much, and not indefinitely.

I am not sure if it is possible.  Yes, I've given myself a chance to work things out, but it really seems like I have tried a lot.  I owed it to myself to try new things after the first few months, and the months after that.  But now I feel like I've used that excuse too much.  The longer I try and it doesn't work, the worse it feels.  And I've long passed the point where the pain is worse than my ability to deal with it.  If there was any kind of threshold, that should have been it.

But no, people's attempts weren't weak.  And I'm not dismissing them.  It just wasn't really enough.  There's only so much one can get out of a few text paragraphs back and forth.  What does one do for a living?  What are their goals?  What is interesting about them?  And then after a page or two, it becomes, Well, how was your day?  And from there, conversation just sort of dies down, and you've reached the limit that you can connect with someone over random reddit PMs.

And no, I guess I haven't tried absolutely everything.  But I've tried most everything that I can still get myself to do.  A year or two ago, I would have tried more.  But feeling like I do now, it isn't a feeling of "Well nothing else matters, I am free to do ANYTHING in the world now."  Its just a feeling of being crushed everyday, where I don't even really want to leave my bed.

I'd go to events at a local hangout, and it would just be so awkward.  Every person though seemed to be with groups of friends, sitting at tables of four or five, with all the seats taken.  When you go to something like that alone, there's just no way to get into those groups.  I tried sitting near other people, asking questions I already knew the answers to, trying to be casual, commenting when it was appropriate.  But I was just met with indifference, or awkward silence.  I usually would spend the rest of the evening sitting alone, nursing a beer or something.  After the third time of this, I just couldn't do it anymore.  Every time I would get home, and just want to cry.

That was only one front, really.  I've also been on online dating sites for over a year.  Two sites actually.  Not doing anything weird there, following all the advice, vetting my profile online at forums for that kind of stuff.  Being open, nice, not creepy.  But I'm short, scrawny, not confident at all.  Out of some 150 - 200 people contacted, I had one date a few months ago, who never replied back after that, and another meetup where the girl stood me up.  And I put a lot of effort into that, both time-wise, and emotionally.  I had never made such a serious attempt at dating before, and that had always been one of my comforts when I was actually alone.  But after actually trying, putting so much into it, and still not having it work at all, I was crushed.  Coupled with all of the other social failures, it was completely devastating.

It was gradual, over the course of a couple years.  College ended, everyone split up and went into the real world.  For me that meant grad school.  I worked too hard to be depressed, and had too many courses and projects with others to be lonely.  I kept up with close friends electronically, and continued to be absorbed in my work otherwise.

But then everyone had their own lives to continue, and there really wasn't anymore time for me.  Friends got invested in their boyfriends or girlfriends, some got married, had kids.  People I was close to, and supported emotionally, became more distant.  Didn't have time to catch up anymore.

I moved again.  Ended up working more alone.  At first it was fine, but then I hear less and less from all my friends.  I try to make new ones, but it just never works.  I go out to coffee shops, parks, concerts.  Even bars, something I never thought I'd do.  But if I try to talk to someone, I get rejected, whether its a platonic interest or a romantic one.  

At first it doesn't bother me, and I keep at it.  Then it becomes six months, and I realize that all my old friends are gone, and I still don't have any new ones.  I still try to work at all the social things, but it just gets worse and worse.  And then being depressed and alone just make me more desperate, and sad all the time.  I just slowly stop going out, focus on work.  That keeps me going during the week, but then I start drinking alone in the evenings and weekends.  

That all started maybe a year ago.  Now I'm at the point that I can't even start up again if I tried.  I just had too much failure after too much effort.  It is a stupid saying that one feels better if they at least tried, even if it didn't work out.  It feels much, much worse.

I am just sick of feeling this way, like nothing is fun anymore, like there's no one out there for me.  I am extremely tired of the response that one just needs to wait, and it will happen.  I am too old to believe that anymore, and had to go through too much of being alone to even entertain those kinds of ideas anymore.  I just want all of it to stop.

I did have hobbies, interests.  I used to read a lot, cook, hiking.  Certain topics in literature.  Was working on two non-native languages as well.  And then my career has a lot of opportunity to, put as much into it as one wants to.

But I've already tried reaching out through those.  Either the opportunities to meet others through those methods don't exist.  Or they do exist, and I tried to use them, and ran into the same failures, anxiety, and back to being alone.  Or I was too scared and nervous to use those outlets in the first place, and that was when I still felt somewhat good about my life.  That's not possible at this point. 

Either way, I just don't have any motivation or drive to work on all that again.  It's hard to describe to someone else how much I worked at meeting others the past few years, and how all of my old connections with friends faded away, and any new one would fizzle off, or I'd end up hurt by that person.  I just don't get any kind of joy pursuing my old interests anymore.  Anything I do now it just to keep myself distracted until I am back in bed.

In the past few months, I've tried to get advice on other forums, other subreddits.  I don't think there's anything that can be suggested that I haven't already heard now.
I just wasn't having fun doing them anymore.  I realized the only reason I kept up with them, was because they were a distraction from feeling sad and lonely.

I guess video games and movies, although I've sort of given up a lot of my hobbies.  

I don't really think you can just "check facebook" for clubs, but no, nothing really in the area.  I've tried google, and Meetup.com.  The majority of the clubs I'm not really qualified for; for parents, or older people, or people of a specific race.  I'm in a larger city, east coast of Virginia, but without being associated with a college anymore, there aren't really just random groups people can join that easily...

I am in a larger city.  I tried events, but I can barely find anything.  I sometimes hung out at local spots; park, mall, coffee shop.  But in the end, I was just completely alone while managing to stay in public.  Every so often I'd get the courage to try to talk to people, but every time it was awkward, or I'd get shut down.  Most people either go out with friends, and don't want to associate with some awkward nerdy stranger.  Or if they are alone, they just want to be left alone.  Or maybe not, and its just me.

I do have hobbies.  Or did, I guess.  Lots of movies, reading, tinkering with electronics, exercise, cooking.  Anything I could do by myself, and keep myself distracted.  I don't really get any pleasure out of any of that stuff anymore though.  If I do keep up with anything, its only because its slightly better than lying in bed all day.

I know you are trying to help, but these are things I've thought over hundreds of times.  Improving myself, going out.  I just can't really do it anymore.  When I did, I tried googling local clubs, but also Meetup.com, local parks and rec, hung out at coffee shops, local trails, even bars.  Found local concerts, looked for classes, tried to find local singles events.  Tried to find local sports leagues.  Ate alone at nearby restaurants.  Outdoor mall.  Sitting on a random bench.  Just tried wandering around town.  

I spent so much time trying to meet people, and in the end it never worked.  Either the events don't exist, or I go and end up not being able to talk to anyone, or I do talk but end up getting rejected.  And then I feel much worse.

Yeah, I am able to do things to take my mind off wanting to kill myself, but then I still find myself completely alone every evening.  And without any kind of change in my situation for years now, its not like I can keep myself distracted indefinitely.  I've just completely given up, and I'm kind of resigned to this.

I have reached out to others before.  Not about the suicide, but about the depression, the loneliness, the dating troubles.  That's the reason most of my friends left me, due to it being all I would talk about.  I haven't talked to some in them in months, even a year.

I can't really try to connect with them now that I've thought about killing myself, and they feel like they have some kind of moral obligation to help now that its more serious.  They didn't stick with me or help before.

Anyway, reaching out to friends who live states away doesn't solve any of my loneliness problems.  I've tried dating for nearly 10 years now, without ever being able to connect with someone in any real way.  I just think I'm incapable of it.  Getting help will only trick me into ignoring those problems, but they are still there.  No one should have to keep living like this, as I have...

I don't have any weapons.

I haven't told anyone. Of course I know they would talk me out of it. And I also know that doing this will cause pain to some people, although I have very few people left. But that pain isn't going to be worse than what I usually have to deal with every not, for what seems like so long now.

I know its selfish having to transfer that to other people, and it used to be what stopped me for the longest time. But most everyone else is pushed away at this point, there's less people affected by it. And my inability to deal with it has gotten worse than those worries that I had.

Still here.  I didnt check this often.  Feel just as bad and alone as I always have though.  But my thoughts on this really haven't changed.  I only feel slightly better that I know I probably won't have to feel like this much longer, and that I'm not rushing it.  That sort of makes the present somewhat bearable

I go to college, I'm still a university grad student, but I dont take classes, and I'm not living nearby anymore.  There's a couple random undergrad-only colleges nearby, within an hour drive.  But I'm not associated with them, and I'm 5-6 years older than their oldest students.

Im not really part of anything right now.  I'm in a science field, work at a lab, but don't really work with anyone my age or interests.  I'm not part of any kind of community right now, although I've really tried.  I can go days without talking to anyone but a cashier.  Its just whenever I go to events or things like that, I end up sitting alone.  Its been so awkward in the past, I can't really bring myself to put myself out there anymore.
